relationships.description: Infliximab binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF with high affinity, inducing apoptosis of TNF-expressing immune cells via Fc-mediated CDC and ADCC
Adalimumab is a fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody that neutralizes both soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha
Certolizumab pegol is a PEGylated anti-TNF Fab fragment that neutralizes TNF without Fc-mediated effects; minimal placental transfer
Golimumab is a fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody with high affinity for soluble and transmembrane TNF; approved for UC
Vedolizumab selectively blocks α4β7 integrin binding to MAdCAM-1 on gut endothelial cells, preventing lymphocyte homing to intestinal mucosa
Ustekinumab binds the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23, simultaneously blocking both Th1 and Th17 pathways
Risankizumab selectively neutralizes the IL-23-specific p19 subunit, blocking Th17/ILC3 responses while preserving IL-12-driven Th1 immunity
Mirikizumab binds the IL-23 p19 subunit, reducing IL-17A, IL-17F, and IL-22 production from Th17 cells and ILC3s in the colonic mucosa
Tofacitinib preferentially inhibits JAK1 and JAK3, blocking signaling downstream of common gamma chain cytokines, type I IFN, and IL-6 family receptors
Upadacitinib is engineered for JAK1 selectivity, blocking IL-6, type I/II IFN, and IL-10 family cytokine signaling with JAK2 sparing
Ozanimod is an S1P receptor modulator selective for S1PR1 and S1PR5; induces S1PR1 internalization, sequestering lymphocytes in lymph nodes
Etrasimod is an S1PR1/4/5 modulator with S1PR3 sparing; prevents lymphocyte egress from lymphoid organs into the gut without bradycardia risk
Natalizumab blocks α4 integrin, preventing both α4β1-VCAM-1 (systemic) and α4β7-MAdCAM-1 (gut) lymphocyte adhesion; restricted due to PML risk
Azathioprine is a prodrug converted to 6-TGN, which incorporates into DNA and inhibits de novo purine synthesis in proliferating lymphocytes
6-Mercaptopurine is directly converted to 6-thioguanine nucleotides that suppress lymphocyte proliferation and induce T cell apoptosis
Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase and AICAR transformylase, leading to adenosine accumulation with anti-inflammatory effects
Mesalamine activates PPAR-gamma in colonic epithelial cells, inhibiting NF-κB and COX-2 pathways with topical anti-inflammatory effects
Budesonide activates the glucocorticoid receptor with high topical potency and ~90% first-pass hepatic metabolism, minimizing systemic exposure
Prednisone binds the glucocorticoid receptor leading to transrepression of NF-κB and AP-1 inflammatory gene programs in immune and epithelial cells
Tacrolimus binds FKBP12 and inhibits calcineurin phosphatase, blocking NFAT dephosphorylation and IL-2 transcription in T cells
NOD2 frameshift and missense variants confer the strongest genetic risk for Crohn's disease (OR 3.5); homozygosity/compound heterozygosity increases CD risk 20-40 fold
ATG16L1 T300A variant impairs autophagy and Paneth cell function in CD (OR 1.4); key component of the autophagy pathway
IL23R R381Q is a protective variant (OR 0.6) for both CD and UC; IL-23R is a central therapeutic target validated by ustekinumab and p19 inhibitors
IRGM deletion polymorphisms alter autophagy-mediated clearance of adherent-invasive E. coli, specifically associated with Crohn's disease (OR 1.3)
LRRK2 coding variants associated with CD (OR 1.5); regulates autophagy and NF-κB signaling in myeloid and Paneth cells
TNFSF15 (TL1A) polymorphisms strongly associated with CD (OR 1.4); drives stricturing and penetrating disease via Th1/Th17 co-stimulation
IL10 polymorphisms associated with both CD and UC (OR 1.2); IL-10 is essential for intestinal immune homeostasis and Treg function
IL10RA loss-of-function mutations cause severe very-early-onset IBD in infants; common variants associated with adult-onset UC and CD
PTPN22 R620W gain-of-function variant associated with Crohn's disease (OR 1.3); shared autoimmune risk across RA, T1D, and SLE
STAT3 polymorphisms associated with both CD and UC (OR 1.3); integrates IL-6, IL-10, and IL-23 signaling in intestinal immune cells
JAK2 polymorphisms associated with both CD and UC; JAK2 is a critical signaling hub for IL-6, IL-12, and IL-23 receptors in the gut
IL12B (p40) polymorphisms associated with CD and UC; the p40 subunit is the therapeutic target of ustekinumab
CARD9 polymorphisms strongly associated with both CD and UC; mediates innate immune responses to gut fungi and bacteria via NF-κB activation
NKX2-3 polymorphisms associated with both CD and UC; regulates MAdCAM-1 expression, the ligand for the α4β7 integrin targeted by vedolizumab
MST1 polymorphisms associated with CD and UC; MSP-RON signaling regulates macrophage function and intestinal epithelial wound healing
FUT2 non-secretor status is protective against CD (OR 0.75); determines mucosal glycosylation and gut microbiota composition
HNF4A polymorphisms associated with UC; maintains intestinal tight junction integrity and epithelial barrier function
CCR6 polymorphisms associated with CD; directs Th17 cell migration to CCL20-expressing inflamed intestinal mucosa
SMAD3 polymorphisms associated with CD and UC; mediates TGF-beta-driven Treg induction and Th17/Treg balance in the gut
SLC22A5 variants in the IBD5 risk haplotype associated with Crohn's disease (OR 1.3); OCTN2 carnitine transporter in colonic epithelium
TYK2 protective variant P1104A reduces IL-12/IL-23 signaling and decreases IBD risk; shared genetic risk with psoriasis and SLE
ICOSLG polymorphisms associated with CD and UC; ICOS-ICOSLG interaction drives T follicular helper responses in gut-associated lymphoid tissue
IL-23R is the receptor for IL-23; R381Q protective variant reduces IL-23 signaling and Th17 expansion in the gut
IL-12B encodes the shared p40 subunit of IL-12 and IL-23; essential for Th1 and Th17 differentiation
TYK2 mediates IL-23 receptor signaling through STAT3 activation; P1104A protective variant reduces IL-23 pathway activity
JAK2 couples IL-6, IL-12, and IL-23 receptors to STAT3/STAT4 activation in intestinal immune cells
STAT3 is the central transcription factor for IL-6, IL-10, IL-22, and IL-23 signaling; drives Th17 differentiation and epithelial repair
TYK2 is a JAK family kinase mediating type I IFN, IL-12, and IL-23 signaling; protects against IBD through reduced pathway activity
NKX2-3 regulates MAdCAM-1 expression on gut endothelial cells, controlling α4β7 integrin-mediated lymphocyte homing to intestinal mucosa
CCR6 directs Th17 and Treg migration to CCL20-expressing intestinal epithelium, regulating mucosal immune cell trafficking
TL1A (TNFSF15) binds DR3 to co-stimulate Th1 and Th17 effector cells, amplifying TNF-mediated mucosal inflammation and fibrosis
CARD9 is an adaptor downstream of dectin-1 that activates NF-κB and MAPK pathways, integrating fungal and bacterial signals with TNF responses
NOD2 senses bacterial MDP, recruits ATG16L1 to the plasma membrane, and activates autophagy for intracellular bacterial clearance and Paneth cell defensin secretion
ATG16L1 is essential for autophagosome formation; T300A risk variant is cleaved by caspase-3, impairing autophagy in intestinal epithelium
IRGM regulates autophagy-mediated clearance of adherent-invasive E. coli; deletion polymorphisms impair bacterial autophagy in CD
IL-10 is the master anti-inflammatory cytokine in the gut; suppresses IL-12, IL-23, and TNF production from dendritic cells and macrophages
IL-10RA is the ligand-binding receptor for IL-10; loss-of-function mutations cause severe VEO-IBD due to absent IL-10-mediated immune regulation
Anti-TNF biologic approved for moderate-severe CD and UC; first biologic approved for IBD
Fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody approved for moderate-severe CD and UC; self-administered subcutaneously
PEGylated anti-TNF Fab fragment approved for moderate-severe CD; only anti-TNF suitable throughout pregnancy
Fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody approved for moderate-severe UC; monthly subcutaneous maintenance
Gut-selective anti-α4β7 integrin biologic approved for moderate-severe CD and UC; superior to adalimumab for UC in VARSITY trial
Anti-IL-12/23 p40 biologic approved for moderate-severe CD and UC; effective in anti-TNF failures
Selective anti-IL-23 p19 biologic approved for moderate-severe CD; superior to ustekinumab in SEQUENCE head-to-head trial
Selective anti-IL-23 p19 biologic approved for moderate-severe UC; first IL-23 p19 inhibitor for UC
Oral JAK1/JAK3 inhibitor approved for moderate-severe UC; rapid onset within 3 days; first oral small molecule for UC
Oral selective JAK1 inhibitor approved for moderate-severe CD and UC; first JAK inhibitor approved for CD
Oral S1PR1/S1PR5 modulator approved for moderate-severe UC; first S1P receptor modulator approved for IBD
Oral S1PR1/4/5 modulator approved for moderate-severe UC; second-generation S1P modulator without first-dose monitoring requirement
Anti-α4 integrin biologic approved for moderate-severe CD refractory to anti-TNF; restricted use (TOUCH program) due to PML risk
Thiopurine immunomodulator for steroid-sparing maintenance in CD and UC; requires TPMT genotyping before initiation
Thiopurine antimetabolite for maintenance of remission in CD and UC; alternative to azathioprine for GI intolerance
Folate antagonist immunomodulator for steroid-dependent CD maintenance; second-line after thiopurines
Topical aminosalicylate; first-line for mild-moderate UC induction and maintenance; also used for pouchitis and microscopic colitis
Gut-targeted corticosteroid with high first-pass metabolism for mild-moderate ileocecal CD; superior safety to prednisone
Systemic corticosteroid for rapid induction of remission in moderate-severe CD and UC flares; bridge to immunomodulator or biologic
IV calcineurin inhibitor as rescue therapy for severe steroid-refractory UC; bridge to avoid emergency colectomy
Calcineurin inhibitor for refractory UC and perianal CD; oral or topical rectal formulation; alternative to cyclosporine
The IL-23/Th17 axis is the dominant inflammatory pathway in IBD; drives pathogenic Th17 and ILC3 responses in the intestinal mucosa
JAK-STAT signaling integrates multiple IBD-relevant cytokines (IL-6, IL-12, IL-23, IL-10, IFN); drives mucosal inflammation and systemic responses
α4β7-MAdCAM-1-mediated lymphocyte trafficking drives pathogenic T cell accumulation in the intestinal lamina propria
TNF-alpha signaling drives intestinal inflammation, increases epithelial permeability, and amplifies cytokine cascades in the IBD mucosa
Defective autophagy and epithelial barrier function enable bacterial translocation and chronic innate immune activation, especially in Crohn's disease
Loss of IL-10-mediated anti-inflammatory signaling leads to unchecked immune activation against gut microbiota; IL10/IL10RA mutations cause VEO-IBD
S1P receptor gradients direct pathogenic lymphocyte egress from lymph nodes into the gut; S1PR modulation is an oral therapeutic strategy for UC
